papers.title: Shaping black hole resonances II: Spectroscopic landscapes and interference in black hole ringdown
papers.abstract:
We map analytically the excitation of Schwarzschild quasinormal modes (QNMs) $C_n$ by oscillatory Gaussian perturbations across the pulse width $\sigma$ and carrier frequency $
u$. The excitation coefficient of each mode is determined by the product of an intrinsic excitation factor and a source-dependent overlap evaluated at the complex QNM frequency. For oscillatory Gaussian perturbations, this overlap is the coherent sum of the positive- and negative-frequency branches of the source, with its amplitude factorizing exactly into a Gaussian spectral envelope and an interference factor. We observe that the excitation amplitude peaks at $
u=\omega_n^{m Re}$ only for narrowband sources. For sufficiently broadband pulses, the maximum lies at $
u=0$, so efficient excitation does not necessarily require matching the carrier and the mode frequency. We observe that the interference between branches, modulates the amplitude only for nonzero $
u$, a feature generic to real oscillatory sources. The prominence of the interference-induced modulation is controlled by the ratio $\omega_n^{m Re}/\omega_n^{m Im}$. The phase separates into a mode-only, a width-only and a $
u$-dependent term, the last generated by the same interference, with $
u=0$ being its unique maximum at fixed width. The analytical predictions are validated against time-domain numerical simulations, showing a relative median error of $\sim 4\%$ for $|C_0|$. For $|C_1|$, the median error is $\sim 16\%$ when $\sigma\leq 5$, increasing to $\sim 36\%$ across the full parameter space. The median phase difference for $n=0$ is $\sim0.14 \,m rad $ and for $n=1$, $\sigma\leq5$ it is $0.34\,m rad$. Our results demonstrate that QNM excitation cannot be understood through frequency matching alone and may provide qualitative insights into more realistic astrophysical scenarios.

papers.title: Less is More: Unbiased Galaxy Clustering from Fewer Merger Trees
papers.abstract: Galaxy clustering could strongly constrain galaxy formation models but is rarely used, because the two-point correlation function (2PCF) requires a complete galaxy catalogue at every point in parameter space. Semi-analytic models (SAMs) process each halo merger tree independently, so running a SAM on $m$ of $k$ disjoint partitions of the trees, each spanning the full box, cuts the cost by $k/m$. Because a halo's galaxies are kept or discarded together, one-halo pairs are diluted less than two-halo pairs, and the naive estimate overstates small-scale clustering by a factor $k/m$. We introduce the Sparse and Unbiased Clustering Estimator (SaUCE), which removes this bias with weights set by $m$ and $k$ alone. It has no free parameters, gives exactly unbiased pair counts, and applies to any catalogue built from a random subset of whole haloes and to any pair-count statistic. Running a SAM on 7 per cent of the P-Millennium merger trees, 68 per cent of random selections recover the full-box $\xi(r)$ at $z=0$ to within 0.05 dex in each bin from 0.03 to $30\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, at a density of $10^{-2}\,h^{3}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$: a fourteen-fold computational saving. The required fraction rises with redshift and as the number density falls, is the same for two model variants, and transfers between boxes through the galaxy and pair counts. The scatter, derived in closed form, is strongly correlated between bins, so a likelihood must use the full covariance. A recipe for choosing the fraction makes the 2PCF affordable for model calibration and simulation-based inference.
papers.comments: 15 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to MNRAS

papers.title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology
papers.abstract: Quantum gravity arguments such as trans-Planckian censorship suggest that de Sitter space can only last for a time of order $H^{-1}\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H)$, corresponding to the fast-scrambling time of black hole and cosmological horizons. We ask whether this clock leaves an imprint on cosmic expansion, via a minimal modification of the Raychaudhuri equation that adds a term $-\Gamma H^2/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ to $\dot H$, with $\Gamma={\cal O}(1)$. The slowly varying $\sigma\equiv\Gamma/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)\ll 1$ is nearly constant at late times. De Sitter space is replaced by a slowly evolving vacuum (an exact Lambert-$W$ solution), and for constant $\sigma$ the expansion rate is found in closed form for arbitrary matter sources. The correction acts as dark energy with two components: a vacuum mode with $w=-1+2\sigma/3$, and a term that integrates over the history of the cosmic fluids, so that any change in the equation of state of a species leaves a permanent residual; e.g., neutrinos becoming non-relativistic shift the dark energy density by ${\cal O}(\sigma m_\nu^4)$. A covariant clock-field completion reproduces this background, and a term that rescales the gravitational constant governing cosmic expansion removes its short-wavelength instability in the dark-energy era. Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints give a proxy bound $\Gamma=-3.7\pm6.1$ (68% confidence), while the negative-$\Gamma$ branch qualitatively follows the $w_0w_a$CDM dark energy evolution inferred from DESI DR2 at $z\gtrsim1$. The early-time tracking terms amount to a similar rescaling, for which existing fits to cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) and supernova data translate into the proxy estimate $\Gamma\simeq-2.8\pm0.9$ ($\sigma\simeq-0.01$ today). These background-level results motivate a dedicated likelihood analysis of structure formation in this theory.

papers.title: Revealing Hidden Excitation in the Core of NGC 4696: New Infrared Diagnostic Diagrams with JWST
papers.abstract: The warm molecular and ionized gas in filamentary nebulae of cool-core BCGs provide a sensitive probe of the poorly understood exchange of energy between the ICM, cold molecular gas, and AGN feedback. Optical line ratios commonly yield similar LINER-like classifications across these systems, but do not resolve how the excitation of warm molecular gas varies between compact nuclear structures and surrounding filaments. We present JWST/NIRSpec integral-field spectroscopy of the central $3''\times3''$ ($620\times620~{\rm pc^2}$) of the Centaurus cluster BCG, NGC~4696. The NIR data resolve H$I$ and ro-vibrational H$_2$ emission across compact nuclear apertures, a circumnuclear swirl, and filamentary structures. H$_2$ excitation diagrams yield characteristic low-excitation temperatures of $T_{\rm ex}\simeq1.8-2.2\times10^3$~K, while curvature at higher energies requires hotter or non-thermal components. The H$_2$/Pa$\alpha$ balance varies strongly: filamentary regions have H$_2$ 1-0 S(1)/Pa$\alpha$ ratios 4-8 times higher than the compact nuclear apertures. In contrast, matched-aperture optical diagnostic diagrams show substantially less regional separation, with all regions occupying a low-ionization locus. We thus introduce new spatially resolved NIR diagnostic diagrams that reveal distinct molecular excitation conditions across the nucleus, swirl, and filaments. Ratios are broadly consistent with contributions from AGN-related photoionization, ICM-related cooling radiation, and non-radiative heating, although the present data do not uniquely determine their relative importance. These results demonstrate how spatially resolved NIR spectroscopy reveals excitation variations hidden in conventional optical classifications, providing a new route to constrain the multiphase cooling-feedback cycle in cluster cores.

papers.title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers
papers.abstract: Dark matter over-densities around massive black holes, known as dark matter spikes, can dephase gravitational waves emitted by intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs/EMRIs), offering a promising way to indirectly detect dark matter. This detection channel, however, requires the spike to survive over cosmological time-scales. We investigate the impact that a host black hole's merger history has on its dark-matter spike. We focus on how the inspiral of a massive-black-hole (MBH) binary modifies and disrupts these spikes within the central $\sim 100$ Schwarzschild radii of the black hole. We find that a single merger with mass ratio $q = 0.03$ is capable of reducing a spike's density by around 3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) Schwarzschild radii across all polar angles relative to the binary's plane, independent of the primary MBH's mass, with larger mass ratios inducing even stronger depletion. In fact, a single past merger with mass ratio as small as $q = 0.005$ reduces central densities by 2--3 orders of magnitude, making gravitational-wave dephasing difficult to detect. We relate these results to the MBH merger history by analysing cosmological simulation data from Horizon-AGN. We find that mergers become increasingly common as the MBH mass increases, with mergers of mass ratio q > 0.03 having occurred in 50% of MBHs of mass $3\times10^7M_\odot$ and 95% of mass $10^8M_\odot$ at z=0. These fractions are reached at even lighter masses ($2\times10^7M_\odot$ and $5\times10^7M_\odot$, respectively) at z=3. We find that accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in {\tt Horizon-AGN}. Thus, in combination with previous studies of EMRI-induced depletion, this work constrains the mass range over which massive black holes can host detectable DM spikes to $10^6M_\odot$--$5 \times 10^7M_\odot$ for $z \leq 3$.

papers.title: Dust Reverberation Mapping of Low-Mass Active Galactic Nuclei
papers.abstract: We perform a systematic dust reverberation mapping study of low-mass ($M_{\mathrm{BH}}\sim10^6$-$10^7 M_\odot$) active galactic nuclei (AGNs) selected from a literature-compiled catalog, using data from the Zwicky Transient Facility and the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer. Through quality assessments, we obtain a core sample of 65 sources with W1- and W2-band lag measurements relative to optical light curves. The W2-band lags are generally longer than the W1-band lags, with a median ratio of $\tau_{\mathrm{W2}}/\tau_{\mathrm{W1}}=1.24^{+0.33}_{-0.21}$. We further investigate the relations between dust radius and AGN luminosity ($R_{\mathrm{dust}}-L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$), using different lag measurements and luminosity proxies. Combining our sample with a higher-luminosity AGN sample, we establish unified $R_{\mathrm{dust}}-L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$ relations spanning nearly seven orders of magnitude in bolometric luminosity. The slopes are $0.47\pm0.01$ and $0.44\pm0.01$ for the W1 and W2 bands, slightly below the expectation of $0.5$ from dust radiative equilibrium. In the combined sample, the lag deviations show a negative correlation with Eddington ratio, potentially related to the self-shadowing effect of slim disks. The luminosity-dependent SED variations revealed by the SPHEREx composite spectra suggest that individual luminosity proxies may not fully trace the intrinsic dust-heating luminosity. Both effects may contribute to the shallow $R_{\mathrm{dust}}-L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$ slopes. Future joint optical and near-infrared monitoring with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will further extend dust RM studies to lower-luminosity AGNs hosting lower-mass black holes.

papers.title: Giant Radio Galaxies from the Third Data Release of the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS-DR3): Physical Characteristics and Environments
papers.abstract: Giant radio galaxies (GRGs) are radio-loud active galactic nuclei (AGN) with projected linear sizes exceeding 0.7 Mpc, offering insights into the evolution of large-scale radio jets and their environments. We present 2333 GRGs from the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey Data Release 3 (LoTSS-DR3), with projected sizes of 0.7-2.9 Mpc, redshifts of $0.126 \leq z \leq 3.517$, and 150-MHz radio luminosities of $1.72 \times 10^{24}$-$3.04 \times 10^{28}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Of these, 726 ($\sim 31\%$) lie at $z \geq 1$. We investigate their radio properties, lobe energetics, equipartition pressures, black hole masses, mid-infrared colours, and environments. Equipartition pressure decreases with increasing projected size, consistent with declining lobe energy density as radio structures expand, while its positive correlation with redshift persists after controlling for radio power and projected size. WISE colours highlight the diversity of the host-galaxy population, with approximately 75% of sources with available photometry falling within the empirical AGN/HERG region. For BCG-hosted GRGs, physical projected size shows no significant dependence on cluster mass. Although the normalized projected half-size, $D/(2r_{500})$, decreases with increasing cluster mass, this trend is consistent with the expected self-similar scaling of cluster radius rather than an independent suppression of radio-source growth in massive clusters. The substantial high-redshift population provides an opportunity to investigate GRGs at early cosmic epochs, although surface-brightness dimming and inverse-Compton losses against the cosmic microwave background can limit their detectability.

papers.title: TITAN DR1: The Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe - Host Galaxies I: Associations, Redshifts and Derived Properties
papers.abstract: We present the host-galaxy catalogue for TITAN DR1, a sample of 8378 spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) at $z \lesssim 0.15$ -- the largest homogeneous low-redshift SN Ia sample assembled to date. We describe the association of each SN with its host, the compilation of redshifts, measurements of uniform far-ultraviolet to mid-infrared (FUV--MIR) photometry, and the derivation of host properties through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. Combining four host-association methods with manual vetting, we securely identify hosts for 7856 SNe~Ia (93.8\%). We compile host-galaxy spectroscopic redshifts for 5522 objects and provide CMB-frame and peculiar-velocity-corrected redshifts. \rev{PSF-matched} photometry is measured for 7568 host galaxies, including both global fluxes and local optical-only fluxes within a fixed 1.5~kpc aperture centred on the SN; \texttt{Bagpipes} returns successful global fits for \rev{all} hosts and local fits for 7329. Stellar mass and rest-frame $g-z$ colour are robustly measured from optical data alone, whereas reliable estimates of star-formation rate, dust attenuation, and mass-weighted age require broader wavelength coverage to break age--dust degeneracies\rev{, and are reported for 5827 hosts}; in our redshift range, MIR data suffice and far-IR coverage is not required. The hosts span a representative low-redshift galaxy population, with a median stellar mass of $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)=10.22$ (\rev{60\%} high-mass; $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)>10$), \rev{71\%} star-forming ($\log_{10}(\mathrm{sSFR}/\mathrm{yr}^{-1}) > -10.5$), and an approximately exponential $A_V$ distribution. This catalogue provides the foundation for forthcoming analyses of the luminosity step and the broader role of galaxy environment in SN~Ia standardization and cosmology.

papers.title: Eccentricity greatly enhances the detectability of line-of-sight acceleration in gravitational wave signals
papers.abstract: Compact object binaries formed dynamically are characterized by a tail of eccentric sources and by the potential presence of environmental perturbations. Here we show that the presence of eccentricity in a gravitational-wave (GW) signal strongly enhances the sensitivity to environmental effects, focusing in particular on line-of-sight acceleration (LSA). We demonstrate that this enhancement is recovered in Fisher-analysis forecasts and, crucially, persists in full Bayesian parameter estimation using state-of-the-art eccentric waveform models. The key insight is that the signal should be analyzed from the moment the first detectable eccentric harmonic enters the detector band, rather than from the customary entry of the $n=2$ harmonic: this allows to probe the early inspiral and thus a longer signal, over which the GW dephasing introduced by LSA becomes substantially larger. We show that with this approach constraints on LSA can increase by more than an order of magnitude between eccentricities at 20~Hz $e_{20}=0$ and $e_{20}\sim0.1$, for signals with sufficient signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR), while we predict a factor $5$ amplification even for low-SNR ones. Fully exploiting this effect necessitates the continued improvement of efficient eccentric waveform models and likelihood evaluations, enabling the efficient analysis of signals lasting thousands of seconds and containing a large number of harmonics.

papers.title: Intermediate-redshift slow rotators as the progenitors of the most massive galaxies at z $\sim$ 0
papers.abstract: We study the resolved stellar kinematics and star formation histories, and their dependence on the environment, in a sample of 218 intermediate redshift (0.1 < z < 1) galaxies located in the CANDELS and COSMOS fields, observed with VLT/MUSE. The sample covers galaxies with stellar masses ranging M_star ~10^8 - 10^12 M_sun, including both star-forming and quiescent systems. For 113 galaxies, found in dense environments of galaxy groups, we derive the spin parameter ($\lambda_{R}$), while for the rest of the sample, we use data from previous papers in this series. Given that the surveys used in this work are flux-limited, the $\lambda_{R}$ distribution of our full sample lacks the bimodality observed in the local Universe, but the subsample of galaxies at z < 0.6 resembles the galaxy population in the nearby Universe, in terms of mass, sizes, and stellar population properties, more than galaxies at z > 0.6. We classified the galaxies into fast and slow rotators, finding that ~8% (17/218) of the galaxies are slow-rotating. The fraction of slow rotators does not change significantly down to z = 0, but we find that in the z ~ 0 sample, the spin parameter is, on average, higher than at higher redshifts. In our subsample at z > 0.6, we observed evidence for the existence of the kinematic morphology-density relation. The slow rotators in our sample mostly assemble their stellar mass in one or two main episodes of formation, and they finished assembling their mass via star formation by redshift of z $\sim$ 1. It is however, not clear if the loss of angular momentum can be associated with the last star formation episode. Based on their location in the mass - size diagram, the intermediate-redshift galaxies are consistent with being the progenitors of the most massive slow rotators observed at z~0, where the subsequent growth is facilitated through gas-poor (dry) mergers.

papers.title: Polarized Equatorial Emission around Kerr Black Holes with Synchronized Scalar Hair. II. Indirect images
papers.abstract: We investigate the intensity polarization properties of the indirect images of a geometrically and optically thin accretion disk around fully self-consistent models of Kerr black holes with synchronized scalar hair. The presence of a massive, self-gravitating scalar field can dramatically alter the lensing properties of the spacetime, resulting in morphologically complex indirect images. We show that for a representative high scalar charge model, this results in the presence of high order central ring-like images at low observer inclinations. These images are not exponentially demagnified, and their polarized intensity, relative to the direct images, is significant. We therefore conclude that the observational signature of strongly scalarized Kerr black holes may not be dominated solely by the $n=1$ image, as images with $n\geq2$ may also contribute significantly to the observed polarized emission, depending on the radial emissivity profile of the disk and the observer inclination.

papers.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes
papers.abstract: Understanding when gravitational collapse produces a black hole remains a central challenge in general relativity. Black-hole uniqueness results characterize the stationary endpoint under suitable assumptions, while singularity theorems establish geodesic incompleteness in the presence of trapped surfaces and appropriate energy and global conditions. Neither, however, provides a general criterion for horizon formation. The hoop conjecture offers such a criterion by relating the enclosed mass to the compactness of a matter distribution in every direction. We construct axisymmetric families of initial data describing rotating dust and test a formulation of the conjecture adapted to this setting. We explore highly prolate and oblate configurations with both constant and differential rescaled angular-velocity profiles, including configurations near the threshold for apparent-horizon formation. We find that the conjecture holds for rotating configurations, with a coefficient within 14% of unity as in the nonrotating case, provided the quasilocal mass includes the rotational energy. If the irreducible mass of the apparent horizon is used instead, the deviations grow with spin, as they do for Kerr black holes. For horizonless configurations, the conjecture likewise holds when the mass is restricted to the energy enclosed by the matter surface, whereas using the ADM mass, which also includes rotational field energy outside the matter, leads to apparent violations of up to $\approx$25%. We also discuss the possible evolution of compact configurations without apparent horizons, their relation to weak cosmic censorship, and their implications for horizonless compact objects.

papers.title: Viscosity heats, diffusion drains: Open-system thermodynamics in unimodular cosmology
papers.abstract: In GR with bulk viscosity and in unimodular gravity with energy diffusion, the matter sector is non-adiabatic, and their balance, entropy, and temperature equations match if $\Pi \leftrightarrow \dot{Q}/3H$. Disagreement over whether unimodular cosmology is adiabatic comes from assigning entropy to matter only or to the total effective fluid. The key is the temperature $T_D$ of the sector absorbing the diffused energy: comoving entropy production is $\dot{Q}(1/T_D-1/T_m)$, yielding earlier limits for $T_D \rightarrow \infty$ and $T_D \rightarrow T_m$. For finite $T_D$, diffusion acts like heat exchange with an external reservoir: unlike viscosity, which only heats a closed fluid, diffusion into a colder bath can cool an open one, breaking the viscosity-diffusion correspondence for observables and stability. Cosmographically, $\Pi$ is fixed by the deceleration $q$, while diffusion is fixed by the jerk $j$; thus $\Lambda$CDM is the adiabatic limit of unimodular cosmology but remains dissipative when modeled via viscosity. The diffusive analogue of $|\Pi|/\rho$ is the shift $c_s^2-\omega$ in effective sound speed, set by perturbative stability rather than acceleration. If dark matter is a gas with conserved rest mass, consistent diffusion removes only thermal energy, forbids phantom behavior, and bounds the growth of the cosmological term by the finite thermal reservoir; producing a logotropic dark fluid with conserved particle number would require relativistic dark matter at $z\simeq12$. With the Hayward-Kodama apparent-horizon temperature, the generalized second law in unimodular gravity follows from the local one, whereas for bulk viscosity it must be imposed separately.

papers.title: Millimeter-Wavelength Constraints on Circular Polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background at Arcminute Scales with the Simons Array
papers.abstract: We present constraints on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) circular polarization anisotropy at arcminute angular scales, using dedicated measurements from the Simons Array taken with a quarter-wave plate and rotating half-wave plate. A detection of circular polarization in the CMB would probe a range of proposed generation mechanisms, from Standard Model astrophysics to physics beyond it. At an observing frequency of 90 GHz, we place constraints over the multipole range $300 \leq \ell \leq 2000$, corresponding to angular scales of 5.4-36 arcmin, in bands of width $\Delta \ell = 100$, roughly tripling the highest multipole previously reached by a $V$-mode power spectrum measurement. Within this domain, we constrain the 95% confidence upper bound of $\ell (\ell+1) C_\ell^{VV} / (2\pi)$ to range from ${\sim}22\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 350$ bandpower to ${\sim}3.5\times10^3\,\mu\mathrm{K}_\mathrm{CMB}^2$ at the $\ell = 1950$ bandpower. These limits are derived from ${\sim}2.5$ months of observations of each of two small regions of the sky located away from the Galactic plane, totaling ${\sim}12\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ of effective sky area. Because the methodology of this study marginalizes known foreground contamination, these bounds serve as robust, conservative limits on the true CMB circular polarization signal down to the sensitivity limits of the instrument. Additionally, we provide an experimental and analytical framework for implementing circular polarization observations on other telescopes by utilizing a quarter-wave plate and half-wave plate design.

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.

papers.title: The UV luminosity function at 1.6 < z < 2.2 from UVCANDELS
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of the rest-frame UV luminosity function (LF) of galaxies at $1.6<z<2.2$ using the UVCANDELS F435W imaging data. Restricting our analysis to sources above $30\%$ completeness to minimize uncertainties at the faint end, we construct a catalog of 5,212 galaxies at $1.6<z<2.2$ down to an absolute magnitude of $M_{\rm UV} = -16.8$, using well-tested photometric redshifts. We perform a maximum likelihood estimate to derive the best-fit Schechter parameters of the UV LF at a median redshift of $z\sim1.9$. We report a best-fit faint-end slope of $\alpha = -1.586 \pm 0.042$. Splitting the sample into two redshift bins, we obtain $\alpha=-1.488 \pm 0.055$ at $z\sim1.75$ and $\alpha=-1.604 \pm 0.066$ at $z\sim2.05$ ($\sim1.4\sigma$ difference), alongside a $\sim2.3\sigma$ brightening in $M^{*}$. Integrating our best-fit LF down to $M_{\rm UV} = -15$, we derive $\rho_{\rm UV} = (1.821 \pm 0.037) \times 10^{26}\ \rm erg\ s^{-1}\ Hz^{-1}\ Mpc^{-3}$ at $z\sim1.9$. Combining our F435W measurements with previous UVCANDELS F275W results and other literature data, we model the redshift evolution of $\rho_{\rm UV}$ from $z\sim0$ to $z\sim10$.

papers.title: Molecular signatures of shocked gas and enhanced cosmic-ray ionization in supernova remnant W49B revealed by ALMA
papers.abstract: Galactic supernova remnants (SNRs) interacting with molecular clouds (MCs) provide important laboratories for investigating how supernova feedback is transferred to the interstellar medium. We performed observations of the HCO+ J=1-0, 3-2, and 4-3 lines, as well as the CO J=3-2 line, toward the eastern and western regions of SNR W49B using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) and the Atacama Pathfinder Experiment (APEX) telescope. In W49B west, we identify twelve regions with broad-line profiles in both HCO+ and CO emission, with FWHM of 25-60 km/s, providing clear evidence of SNR-MC interaction. These emissions are compact (at $\sim$5 arcsec resolution) and spatially coincident with 2.12~$\mu$m H$_2$ emission, but generally offset from the 1.64~$\mu$m [Fe~II] and radio continuum peaks. Non-LTE analyses yield shocked-gas densities of (0.5-1.6) $\times 10^5$~cm$^{-3}$ and high $N_{\rm HCO+}/N_{\rm CO}$ abundance ratios of (4.2-14.5) $\times 10^{-4}$. Reproducing such high abundance ratios in shocked MCs requires high cosmic ray ionization rates (CRIRs) of a few 10$^{-14}$-10$^{-13}$~s$^{-1}$, about 3-4 orders of magnitude above the standard Galactic level. Some regions exhibit enhanced HCO+/CO intensity ratios in their high-velocity line wings, possibly due to multiple unresolved shocks spanning a range of velocities and gas densities, spatial variations in the CRIR, or both. By contrast, the ratio remains nearly constant with velocity in other regions. For these regions, we further explore the propagation of low-energy CRs through the post-shock layer. An energy-budget analysis of a representative shocked clump indicates that the shock-associated kinetic-energy reservoir substantially exceeds cumulative CR and X-ray heating inputs, with CR heating exceeding X-ray heating.[abridged]

papers.title: OASIS: A Fast Dynamical Halo Finding Algorithm
papers.abstract: In recent work (García et al. 2023), we advocated for defining a dynamical halo as the collection of particles that orbit their self-generated potential. Here we introduce the Orbiting-mass ASsIgnment Scheme (OASIS), a fast energy-based algorithm for constructing dynamical halo catalogs. Using single-snapshot information, OASIS achieves $\simeq 9\%$ scatter in orbiting mass estimates relative to the SPARTA particle-tracking algorithm. As an illustration of the applications enabled by OASIS, we use the Quijote and Erebos simulation suites to show that the $z=0$ dynamical halo mass function is nearly universal with respect to cosmology, and that it is well described by a modified Press-Schechter form with an effective collapse threshold $\delta_{\rm sc} = 1.54$ at intermediate masses. However, this description fails at high masses.

papers.title: The unified bound dark energy--bound dark matter model confronted with DESI DR2, ACT and SPT-3G, and the Unite supernovae measurements
papers.abstract: The unified bound dark energy-bound dark matter (BDE-BDM) model derives the whole dark sector from a single supersymmetric SU(3) dark gauge group, whose lightest meson is the dark energy and whose heavier bound states, created with a velocity $v_c$ when the group condenses, are the dark matter. Because the condensation scale $\Lambda_c$ is fixed by gauge-coupling unification, the dark-energy sector has no free parameter beyond those of $\Lambda$CDM, and the dark-matter sector adds only $v_c$. We confront the model with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), the Planck, ACT DR6 and SPT-3G D1 CMB spectra, the combined ACT and SPT CMB lensing and the Unite supernovae. The measured condensation scale, $\Lambda_c=43.74\pm0.11$ eV, lies inside the window $34^{+16}_{-11}$ eV predicted by unification, and the dark energy thaws without ever crossing the phantom divide, reaching $w_0=-0.9267\pm0.0003$ today; it thus reproduces the DESI distances that $w_0w_a$CDM fits with a phantom past. BDE-BDM gives the best fit to the DESI DR2 BAO of the four models, reducing $\chi^2_{\rm BAO}$ by 20% with respect to $\Lambda$CDM, more than $w_0w_a$CDM, and over the full data combination it is statistically equivalent to both $\Lambda$CDM and $w_0w_a$CDM, with $\ln B=-0.50$ and $-0.15$, while having two fewer dark-energy parameters than $w_0w_a$CDM. Within bound dark energy, bound dark matter is moderately preferred over cold dark matter, $\ln B=+3.2$ with $\Delta\chi^2=-9.0$, mostly from the CMB. The data now constrain the bound velocity from both sides, $v_c=0.37\pm0.14$, which places the free-streaming cutoff of the matter power spectrum at $k_{1/2}=1.49\,h$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and lowers the amplitude of structure to $S_8=0.807\pm0.007$. Future high-redshift and Lyman-$\alpha$ forest data, together with growth and lensing measurements, will therefore provide the decisive tests of the unified dark sector.

papers.title: Quasinormal overtones and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar quasinormal modes (QNMs), with particular attention to overtones, and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes, which interpolate between the Reissner--Nordström (RN) and Hayward limits. Over the allowed ranges of charge $q$ and regularization parameter $\alpha_0$, all QNM frequencies have negative imaginary parts, confirming stability against scalar perturbations. Increasing either $q$ or $\alpha_0$ can trigger overtone outbursts, with the Frolov threshold shifted to smaller parameter values than in the RN or Hayward cases. Angular momentum does not eliminate the outburst but postpones its onset from $n=1$ at $l=0$ to $n\geq 2$ at $l=1$. Comparisons of the effective potential show that, for $l=1$, charge raises the barrier peak much more strongly than $\alpha_0$, while the clearest deviations from the Hayward and RN references are localized near the horizon. Using the QNM--grey-body correspondence at $l=1$, we find that overtone corrections are essential, and the amended formula substantially outperforms the eikonal truncation. At fixed frequency, both $q$ and $\alpha_0$ suppress transmission, with charge being the dominant factor, consistent with the stronger barrier enhancement under the charge scan.

papers.title: Scalar-Induced Gravitational Waves Probing Phase Transitions in the Standard Model and Beyond
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are unique messengers of physics in the early Universe and possible sources for the observed data from pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). It has been demonstrated that SIGWs have the potential to probe cosmological phase transitions via measurement of the equation of state and sound speed of the cosmic thermal bath, which have non-trivial time dependence during phase transitions. In this work, we improve on existing studies of SIGWs in a time-dependent background with time-dependent initial conditions and an entropy-conserving thermal history of the Standard Model (SM). We provide possible physical explanations for features of the gravitational wave spectrum from phase transitions, the most prominent of which for a scale-invariant curvature spectrum is a step due to entropy dilution. We show that current and future gravitational wave observations across a wide range of frequencies can probe phase transitions in the SM and physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). Signals from the QCD crossover appear around 10 nHz, inside the observable window of PTAs. We perform data analyses using NANOGrav 15-year data, showing a mild preference for the QCD crossover over standard radiation domination for two choices of curvature spectra. BSM phase transitions in the TeV range lead to signals around mHz, which are accessible in future space-based experiments such as LISA, Taiji and TianQin.

papers.title: Self-Interacting Neutrinos in NEDE and DRMD Cosmologies: Posteriors, profiles and evidence using CLiENT
papers.abstract:
A large number of extensions of the $\Lambda$CDM model have been proposed as solutions to the Hubble tension, but they are almost always tested separately. Combinations of such models are rarely studied, and one reason is that their parameter spaces are very costly to explore with standard methods. Here we study a combination of two models which have each been proposed as a solution: self-interacting neutrinos (SI$
u$) and the dark radiation matter decoupling (DRMD) of hot new early dark energy. The SI$
u$+DRMD model has twelve cosmological parameters, a bimodal posterior in the neutrino self-interaction and several flat directions in parameter space, and it can only be investigated in detail because we use the likelihood emulator CLiENT. With emulators trained on about $3	imes 10^5$ likelihood evaluations per dataset we obtain posteriors, best fits and profile likelihoods for the model and for the models nested within it, and all quoted $\chi^2$ values are calculated with the true likelihood. We use two data combinations, both with and without the SH0ES calibration: a conservative one consisting of Planck, DESI BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more aggressive one in which the small-scale CMB spectra come from ACT and SPT. With the most aggressive combination, the SI$
u$+DRMD model provides a much better fit than either SI$
u$ or DRMD on its own, and its posterior gives $H_0 = 70.94\pm 0.60$ km/s/Mpc. It lowers the $\chi^2$ of $\Lambda$CDM by 27.6, compared with 9.9 for DRMD and 4.0 for SI$
u$, i.e. by more than the sum of the two ($\Delta$AIC = -15.7 relative to DRMD, in terms of the Akaike information criterion). This shows that combined models can fit the data considerably better than the individual models, and it demonstrates the value of being able to analyse such complex models in detail.

papers.title: Impact of Primordial Magnetic Field-induced Small-scale Power on Non-linear Structure Formation and Cosmic Reionization
papers.abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) can enhance small-scale matter perturbations and alter halo formation and reionization. We evolve PMF-modified initial spectra with collisionless $N$-body simulations and use the halo catalogues as sources for semi-numerical ionization and 21-cm brightness-temperature fields in the saturated spin-temperature limit. We compare $\Lambda$CDM with four PMF models, $B_0=100$, $130$, $150$, and $170\,\mathrm{pG}$, at $n_B=-2.9$. With cosmology and source prescriptions fixed, the PMF models show enhanced small-scale clustering, more early low-mass haloes and earlier reionization. Their volume-averaged reionization midpoints advance by $\Delta z_{50}\simeq0.50$--$2.14$, with changes in ionization morphology and 21-cm power spectra. The Thomson optical depth rises from $\tau_{\rm e}\simeq0.0547$ for $\Lambda$CDM to $0.0595$--$0.0786$. These simulation-relative offsets span $0.66$--$3.28$ times the Planck 2018 uncertainty, $\sigma_\tau=0.0073$, and are not exclusion significances. The common source efficiency $N_{\rm ion}$ is calibrated to a reference history approaching ionization completion near $z\sim6$ and an optical depth close to Planck 2018, without model-specific retuning. We omit subsequent magnetic-field evolution and dissipative magnetic heating. Observational bounds require joint treatment of astrophysical degeneracies and numerical uncertainties.

papers.title: On the Existence of an Equilibrium Density Profile for Massive Collisional Star Clusters
papers.abstract: The dynamical evolution of massive, dense star clusters is governed by a complex interplay of multiple physical processes, including two-body relaxation, strong encounters, stellar evolution, and galactic tides, superimposed on the orbital motion of individual stars and binaries within the cluster potential. These processes can alter the internal evolution of individual stars and binaries, produce exotic stellar objects, and collectively determine the global structural evolution of the cluster. In this paper, we use the Monte Carlo star cluster evolution code CMC-COSMIC to study how the density profiles of dense star clusters evolve under the combined effects of these processes. We find that for a given initial mass and binding energy, cluster models converge toward a characteristic density profile largely independent of their initial density distributions. This convergence occurs during the late-time, quasi-static phase of evolution, when gravitational contraction is balanced by energy generated through black hole binaries in the cluster core. The shape of this profile is well represented by a King profile with W_0=6.8 but with the virial radius of the final cluster larger than the initial by a factor of about 7. We further show that this equilibrium profile is dynamically stable, i.e., perturbations away from it decay through the cluster's natural dynamical evolution, driving the system back toward the equilibrium profile.

papers.title: Stable cosmology under flexible covariances: Rescaling and cross-survey correlations in DESI BAO and supernova data
papers.abstract: Combinations of cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO), and Type Ia supernova (SN) data currently favor evolving dark energy over $\Lambda$CDM at the $\sim 3$--$4\sigma$ level, making it important to test whether this preference could be driven by imperfectly modeled uncertainties. We introduce a phenomenological framework in which the published covariance of each dataset is rescaled by a free parameter and the SN compilations are allowed effective cross-survey correlations. We apply it to DESI DR2 BAO, Planck 2018 temperature and polarization data, and a joint likelihood of Pantheon+, Union3, and DES-Dovekie constructed on a common redshift basis. The DESI, Union3, and DES-Dovekie data are consistent with their published covariances, while Pantheon+ shows a mild preference for additional covariance. In all cases the data still allow error bars up to $\sim 1.7$ times larger than published at 95% credibility, yet freeing the rescaling parameters improves the best fit by $\Delta\chi^2 < 1$. Pantheon+ and Union3 exhibit a clear positive effective correlation, $r\simeq 0.4$--$0.5$, plausibly reflecting their shared supernovae; the Pantheon+--DES-Dovekie correlation is weaker and model dependent, and the Union3--DES-Dovekie correlation is consistent with zero. The added covariance freedom broadens the cosmological constraints without shifting them: for the full data combination, the improvement of $w_0w_a$CDM over $\Lambda$CDM changes only from $\Delta\chi^2 = 12.8$ to $12.3$ (nominally $3.15\sigma$ to $3.07\sigma$). The preference for evolving dark energy is therefore robust to covariance misestimation of the form considered here.

papers.title: Tracing early galaxies back in time: implications for the dearth of galaxies beyond z~15
papers.abstract: Although the James Webb Space Telescope has pushed the observational frontier to $z\sim14$, the onset of star formation in the earliest galaxies remains beyond direct reach, making the star formation histories (SFH) of observed galaxies a key tool for probing earlier epochs. We develop and validate a new SFH model based on an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, capable of reproducing the bursty star formation expected in high-redshift galaxies. Tested on the SPHINX$^{20}$ mock catalogs, it accurately recovers stellar masses and SFRs and reconstructs cumulative SFHs at population level; the formation redshift is well constrained at $z\gtrsim9$ but not at $z\sim8$. Applied to 400 galaxies at $9<z<15$ from the UNICORN/GOODS-South sample, we find that sources observed at $z<10$ typically reached 20% of their stellar mass no earlier than $z\sim12$, disfavoring a clear evolutionary link to spectroscopically confirmed galaxies at $z\gtrsim13$. Among 218 galaxies at $10<z<15$, only 28 had formed 20% of their stellar mass by $z=15$, with a median formation redshift $z_{\rm form,20\%}=16.9^{+1.1}_{-1.1}$, and 24% of our sample had already reached $10^7$M$_{\odot}$ by $z=15$. At $z=17$, only 11 of these 28 galaxies had reached 20% of their stellar mass. The derived survey areas required to detect them are consistent with or slightly more optimistic than previous constraints at the bright end, and larger than some literature estimates at the faint end. At $z=20$, a single galaxy had formed 20% of its stellar mass, yielding a tentative constraint of one object at $M_{\rm UV}=-18.1\pm0.6$ per $\sim200$\,arcmin$^2$. Our results suggest a relatively slow decline in star formation activity between $z\sim15$ and $z\sim17$, followed by a more rapid decline up to $z\sim20$.

papers.title: Deriving physical parameters of unresolved star clusters. X. Size evolution of young star clusters in the M31 disc
papers.abstract: Context. Star cluster structural properties and their correlations with other cluster parameters (age, mass, galactocentric distance) provide key constraints on cluster formation and dynamical evolution within star-forming galactic discs. In the tenth paper of this series, we analysed structural parameters of 1918 young star clusters (up to 800 Myr) in the disc of M31. Aims. We aim to examine the structural evolution of M31 disc clusters and determine how their sizes correlate with physical and spatial properties. Our goal is to improve the understanding of cluster formation and evolution in spiral galaxy discs. Methods. We use the M31 disc cluster parameter catalogue based on photometric measurements of the Panchromatic Hubble Andromeda Treasury survey data. We perform statistical analysis to determine how cluster structural parameters relate to their physical characteristics and location within the disc. Results. Young clusters in the disc of M31 are compact ($R_{50}\sim1.8$ pc) and expand rapidly during the first $\sim$20 Myr, more than doubling in size. At older ages, M31 clusters follow a weak age-radius relation $(R_{50}\propto t^{0.12\pm0.01}\,\,)$. We find no significant correlation between cluster size and galactocentric distance, indicating that internal processes dominate their early evolution, with minimal impact from the galactic tidal field. Our results suggest that stellar-evolution-driven mass loss and internal dynamical interactions are likely drivers of early cluster structural evolution in the M31 disc. A shallow mass-radius relation emerges for clusters older than 100 Myr $(R_{50}\propto M^{0.18\pm0.01}\,\,)$, while the trend for younger clusters remains uncertain. The diversity of mass-radius relations observed in nearby spiral galaxies, both within and beyond the Local Group, highlights the need for further theoretical work on cluster formation and evolution.

papers.title: Measuring the Milky Way potential with the phase snail shape curves
papers.abstract: Aims. Phase spirals found in the vertical phase-space ($z-V_z$) indicate that the Galactic disk is in disequilibrium. Although the origin remains elusive, the wrapping of phase snails is dominated by the vertical potential profiles, naturally encoding potential information in their shapes. Methods. To measure the Galactic potential, we extracted the phase snail shape curves from density contrast maps and transformed them into the vertical frequency-action angle ($\Omega_z - \theta_z$) space via orbital integration, then performed linear fitting to derive potential parameters. We verified our method with a test particle simulation. Results. Our method performs well in the test particle simulation, with the recovered Galactic vertical potential profiles in excellent agreement with the input potential models. We also apply our method to the observed phase snails with guiding center radii in the range of $8\le R_g\le11$ kpc. Utilizing snail shape curves only, the model derived vertical potential profiles agree with popular Milky Way potential models. The model yields a Galactic virial mass of $M_{200}= 0.81^{+0.22}_{-0.23} \times10^{12}\, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ and a local dark matter density of $\rho_{dm,\odot}= 0.0076^{+0.0019}_{-0.0021} \,{\rm M_{\odot}\,pc^{-3}}$, consistent with the literature, but with a flatter rotation curve than the observation. To better constrain the Galactic potential, we further combine the phase snails and the rotation curve. The improved model results in $M_{200}= 0.87^{+0.31}_{-0.33} \times10^{12}\, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ and $\rho_{dm,\odot}= 0.0097^{+0.0002}_{-0.0009} \,{\rm M_{\odot}\,pc^{-3}}$. The high precision of $\rho_{dm,\odot}$ results from the joint constraints in the solar neighborhood. We also obtain an estimation of the perturbation time in a range of 400-750 Myr with a median of 564 Myr, consistent with recent measurements. (abridged)

papers.title: Inverse Scattering & Isospectrality in (Analog) Cosmology
papers.abstract: Cosmological particle production, the excitation of field quanta by a dynamical spacetime, underlies the primordial perturbations observed in the cosmic microwave background and has been realized in analog quantum simulators with ultra-cold atoms. We ask the inverse question: given the excitation spectrum, can the cosmological history that produced it be reconstructed, and is that reconstruction unique? We approach this problem through a mapping of particle production to one-dimensional quantum scattering, in which the expansion history plays the role of a scattering landscape and the produced spectrum the role of reflected and transmitted waves. This mapping reveals a rich interplay between scattering theory and cosmology. The scale factor enters as a zero-energy resonance, an exceptional case of scattering theory, while cosmic singularities correspond to bound states, so that regular cosmologies are governed entirely by the scattering continuum. We find an interesting isospectrality: histories related by an inversion of the scale factor (expansion <-> contraction) yield identical particle numbers, differing only by a pi-shift in phase. Given both the particle number (or alternatively the amplitude) and phase of the cosmological power spectrum, the reconstruction is unique for regular, asymptotically static cosmologies. We demonstrate the reconstruction both analytically, for exactly solvable scattering landscapes, and numerically, recovering common logistic expansion histories to better than 0.02%. We further quantify its robustness to the momentum-space resolution and measurement uncertainties characteristic of analog quantum simulation. This work establishes a direct link between the observable power spectrum and the cosmological history that produced it, offering a new perspective on the classification of early-universe scenarios and the construction of alternatives to inflation.

papers.title: Dust in Stellar Populations: Grid-Based and Bayesian Spectral Energy Distribution Fitting of AGB Stars with SEDust and MCM-SEDust
papers.abstract: Dust shapes the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of stellar populations on every scale, from the circumstellar envelopes of evolved stars to the interstellar medium of galaxies. We discuss how both connect the physics of individual dusty stars to the dust budget of stellar populations.

papers.title: A Virgo Environmental Survey Tracing Ionised Gas Emission (VESTIGE). XXIII. NGC 4569 past orbit reconstruction with ORFEO
papers.abstract: Extended ionised gas tails can preserve a dynamical record of a galaxy's recent interaction with the intracluster medium (ICM). Recovering that history from the observed tail requires solving an inverse dynamical problem tied to the physical conditions for gas removal. We present the first application of ORFEO to NGC 4569, using the sky positions and line-of-sight (LOS) velocities of the galaxy and 94 H$\alpha$-emitting regions to reconstruct its recent orbit and tail chronology. The model combines data with gas surface-density constraints, a spherical Virgo Cluster A gravitational potential derived with MG-MAMPOSSt, and an X-ray-based ICM density profile. For an assumed LOS distance, it infers its orbit and ram-pressure history. At the fiducial distance $d_0=16.5$ Mpc, ORFEO recovers a coherent phase-space sequence with a dynamical tail age $T_{\rm tail}=250^{+37}_{-19}$ Myr. The ram-pressure maximum occurred at $t_{P_{\rm ram},{\rm peak}}=-163^{+11}_{-15}$ Myr, close to the nearest approach to the Virgo Cluster A centre at $305^{+19}_{-25}$ kpc, placing NGC 4569 after peak ram pressure. Scanning the LOS distance does not select a unique solution but separates comparably fitting reconstructions into a low-distance post-peak branch and a high-distance pre-peak branch. Comparison with an independent stripping threshold at the observed disc truncation radius favours the low-distance solutions and supports a post-stripping interpretation. On this branch, ORFEO recovers the mostly west-to-east projected motion inferred from the H$\alpha$ morphology and is consistent with previous constraints on the interaction chronology. Requiring only $\sim10$--11 min of wall-clock time for NGC 4569, ORFEO provides a computationally inexpensive inverse framework for deriving orbital, tail, and ram-pressure histories that can guide tailored simulations and be extended to larger samples of stripped galaxies.

papers.title: Non-singular cosmology from effective LQG-inspired black holes
papers.abstract: We propose a non-singular primordial cosmology derived from matching an effective Loop Quantum Gravity-inspired black hole geometry to an expanding Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker universe via Darmois-Israel junction conditions. The resulting modified Friedmann equation replaces the singularity with a quantum bounce in the Planckian regime. Mapping the surface energy-momentum tensor of the dynamic thin shell onto a homogeneous scalar field reveals a transient phantom-like behavior. For any equation of state of the shell satisfying $\omega > -1$, its effective energy density is diluted with cosmic expansion. Extending the framework to a two-scalar-field system provides a mechanism to bridge the energy gap between the Planckian bounce and the sub-Planckian scale. The pre-inflationary phase is brief, enabling the second scalar field to take over to drive the standard slow-roll inflation.

papers.title: Gravitational Origin of Black Hole Thermodynamic Geometry from Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: In black hole thermodynamics, Hessian metrics change both their signature and their singularities from one statistical ensemble to another. A negative eigenvalue may therefore signal either a physical instability or only a Legendre transformation. We derive this geometry from the bulk action and boundary terms of four-dimensional Euclidean Einstein-Maxwell-anti-de Sitter gravity. In the bulk, the radial symplectic flux pairs the mass and charge with their asymptotic sources, and horizon regularity selects the equilibrium states. At infinity, the boundary terms determine the ensemble polarization by specifying which reservoir parameters are held constant and which conjugate quantities fluctuate. Fixing the temperature and electric potential gives the Ruppeiner metric, whereas adding the Maxwell boundary term fixes the charge and reverses the corresponding metric sign. Tracking the boundary conditions thus separates true stability boundaries from singularities of the Legendre transform. Local holographic counterterms leave the metric unchanged, while mixed electric boundary conditions interpolate between the two ensembles and shift their stability limits.

papers.title: Renormalized dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in binary dynamics
papers.abstract: We present the relativistic dynamical tidal response of a neutron star computed using stellar perturbation theory and matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase. This phase is defined as the difference between the Compton/Raman scattering phase of gravitational-waves from a neutron star and the real part of the black hole scattering phase. The gravitational corrections to the response function are obtained using self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order. The response function for neutron stars obeying the BSk22 equation-of-state from Brussels-Skyrme family, is then consistently matched to an effective theory of relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators to model the fundamental-mode ($f$-mode) and low-frequency gravity-modes ($g$-modes). This matching includes the frequency and tidal coupling of each mode and the post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love number, and once matched this model is in excellent agreement with the full neutron star response. With the external tidal field up to third post-Newtonian order, we also analyse the tidal coupling of the induced quadrupole on the neutron star in a circular binary system, and the adiabatic binding energy.

papers.title: Cosmic String Networks with Time-Varying Tension: Field-Theory Simulations and an Analytic Model
papers.abstract: Cosmic string networks are predicted in some early-Universe scenarios, and in certain models, the string tension becomes a function of time. Here, for the first time, we perform numerical field-theory simulations of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension in an expanding Universe. We use a modified Abelian-Higgs model in which the tension varies as a power law of the scale factor $a$, that is, $\mu \propto a^{-2m}$. We perform simulations on grids containing $8192^3$ grid points, with $m\in[-0.5,0.5]$, during radiation- and matter-dominated epochs. We find that, in our model, a string network forms only when the potential decreases more slowly than the amplitude of field oscillations redshifts due to the expansion of the Universe. Once formed, the network evolves according to the standard scaling behavior predicted by the velocity-dependent one-scale (VOS) model. To interpret these results, we compare the predictions of the VOS model with time-dependent tension to the asymptotic values obtained from the numerical simulations. Overall, we find good agreement between the numerical field-theory simulations and the calibrated VOS model. These results shed light on the evolution of cosmic string networks with time-varying tension and have potential implications for their observational signatures.

papers.title: Simulation-Based Inference on EMRI Frequency Tracks: Harmonic Identification and Parameter Constraints from Search Outputs
papers.abstract: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) are key targets for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but their long, multi-harmonic waveforms make search and parameter estimation computationally expensive. A promising alternative is to work directly with frequency tracks recovered by a time-frequency search pipeline. We investigate whether such tracks can be used to (i) identify which harmonic(s) a recovered track corresponds to, and (ii) constrain the intrinsic EMRI parameters, including when tracks are partially masked near plunge. We first train Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) networks on large banks of azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks. For harmonic identification, we combine pairs of candidate tracks under different harmonic-label assumptions and use the resulting posterior medians and network acceptance rates to classify the correct labelling. For parameter identification, we apply a sequential (truncated-prior) SBI scheme and refine the results by cross-checking posterior samples against a time-frequency detection statistic. The correct harmonic pair is among the top-2 ranked candidates with probability $>0.99$ across masking levels, and is identified outright in 98% of cases when restricted to physically plausible candidates. Sequential SBI shrinks the intrinsic-parameter prior volume by up to $10^{13}$ within a few hours of GPU time, and the detection-statistic refinement reduces it by up to four further orders of magnitude, even for heavily masked tracks. Frequency-track-based SBI thus provides a fast, waveform-free way to identify EMRI harmonics and obtain tight prior volumes for targeted follow-up, substantially reducing the burden on subsequent MCMC-based analyses.

papers.title: Shot noise, aperture and resolution in Fourier measurements of disc lopsidedness: TNG50-1 and TNG100-1 analysed with TNGGalaxyLab
papers.abstract: We present TNGGalaxyLab, an open-source Python pipeline for particle-based Fourier decomposition of the stellar surface density of simulated disc galaxies. Fourier amplitudes are positive-definite, so Poisson noise biases them upwards by an amount that grows as the particle number falls. We measure a per-galaxy noise floor by randomising particle azimuths and define a noise-corrected amplitude A1,corr. Downsampling TNG50-1 discs to the TNG100-1 particle mass inflates the uncorrected A1 by 40-60 per cent, while A1,corr is recovered to within approximately 10 per cent. We then process all central galaxies with 3.16 x 10^9 < M*/Msun < 10^11 in TNG50-1 (915) and TNG100-1 (6717) with identical settings in the [1.5, 2.5] Rd aperture. Removing the bootstrap and shot-noise biases lowers the TNG100/TNG50 ratio of median A1 from 2.3 to 1.6. At fixed stellar mass, kinematically selected TNG100-1 discs remain 1.5-1.9 times more lopsided after correction; this excess persists whether the aperture is defined in Rd or in kpc, is not explained by kappa_rot or D/T, and is largest at 3.5-6 kpc. TNG50-1 is statistically consistent with the mass-matched S4G sample of Zaritsky et al. (2013); TNG100-1 is not. The low A1 reported for TNG100 by Lokas (2022) cannot be read as a resolution deficit, since with matched measurements TNG100-1 is more lopsided than TNG50-1. Code and catalogues are public.

papers.title: Tracing the Epoch of Reionization through extreme emission line galaxies around Cosmic Noon
papers.abstract: Star-forming galaxies at z>6 are thought to be the main drivers of cosmic reionization, but their faintness makes detailed study challenging even with JWST. Extreme Emission Line Galaxies (EELGs) are compact, low-mass systems with intense nebular emission and are potential lower-redshift analogues of this population. We aim to assemble and characterize a statistically significant sample of EELGs in the CANDELS/EGS field around cosmic noon, and to assess their validity as analogues of the galaxies that drove reionization. We select EELG candidates from CANDELS photometry with a J-band color-excess criterion that identifies both H$\beta$+[OIII] and H$\alpha$ emitters. Physical properties are taken from CANDELS data products, and the selection is validated with MMT/MMIRS, Keck/MOSFIRE, HST/WFC3 and JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, complemented by our own GTC/OSIRIS+ program. We identify 102 H$\beta$+[OIII] emitters at $z\sim1.7$ and 127 H$\alpha$ emitters at $z\sim1.0$. They are compact ($\sim$1.6 kpc), low-mass ($\log(M_\star/M_\odot)\sim8$) and strongly star-forming (sSFR $\sim10^{-8}$ yr$^{-1}$). Estimated purities of $84.3\pm1.5$\% (H$\beta$+[OIII]) and $76.8\pm2.0$\% (H$\alpha$) agree with spectroscopic confirmation rates (85\% and 63\%), with no evidence of significant AGN contamination. We spectroscopically confirm a highly pure, AGN-free sample of cosmic-noon EELGs. While their mass scale evolves with redshift, their properties consistently match those of z>5 JWST extreme emitters, supporting them as intermediate-redshift analogues.

papers.title: Dynamical obstructions to primary Proca hair and its logarithmic Maxwell continuation
papers.abstract: We examine the dynamical admissibility of primary black hole hair in a regularized vector theory of Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The original nontrivial constant norm family cannot satisfy both positive dipole kinetic energy and real nondegenerate radial tensor characteristics. A regular Hamiltonian reduction treats the degenerate boundaries. For asymptotically flat exteriors on the nondegenerate radial branch, adding a Maxwell term for the same vector requires a varying norm. Its positive logarithmic continuation has finite mass at spatial infinity and numerically constructed regular future horizons. The constructed backgrounds satisfy the radial tensor and transverse vector conditions at the sampled points. However, the constrained even angular system has a longitudinal mode with negative squared angular speed. We derive its inverse logarithm coefficient, including both the vector constraint and quartic interaction, and verify it using independent gauge reductions and the full backgrounds. This local angular obstruction persists despite the compatible radial conditions.

papers.title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
papers.abstract: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Padé resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

papers.title: Dwarf galaxy simulations with stellar-core mass- and metallicity-dependent core-collapse supernova explosion energies
papers.abstract: Core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) are a critical source of thermal and kinetic energy and chemically enriched material in galaxies. Leveraging recent advances in CCSN modelling, we implement a novel core-mass- and metallicity-dependent prescription for stellar explodability and CCSN explosion energies, $E_\mathrm{expl}$, in the SPHGal galaxy evolution code. It accounts for black hole (BH) formation via SN failures and via partial fallback of ejecta mass, and adopts an explosion-progenitor connection calibrated to three-dimensional CCSN simulations, such that $E_\mathrm{expl}$ varies between $<0.1$-$2\, \mathrm{B}$. We ran simulations of isolated low-metallicity galaxies with variations in the input stellar feedback models. With the new explodability prescription nearly three times more BHs form compared to the canonical CCSN-model, but the reduced number of successful CCSNe has minimal impact on galactic star formation owing to the low fraction of failed CCSNe. While BH formation contributes to removal of matter from the galactic baryon cycle, the latter remains driven by galactic outflows, and most compact remnant mass is stored in white dwarves. The most significant change is instead brought about by the new average-$E_\mathrm{expl}$ that amounts to $\sim33$\% of the $1\,\mathrm{B}=10^{51}\, \mathrm{erg}$ traditionally assumed in sub-resolution CCSN-models. This reduction results in increased and less bursty star formation, reduced outflows and mass-loading factors, increased star cluster formation efficiency, and enhanced chemical enrichment and metal-recycling in star-forming regions. These results stand in contrast with outflow-launching and baryon cycle modelling in lower-resolution galaxy simulations in which canonical (i.e., $1\, \mathrm{B}$) CCSN feedback is typically assumed to produce galaxy models that match observed scaling relations.

papers.title: Connecting field-level and n-point function measurements of galaxy bias
papers.abstract: Precise measurements of galaxy bias parameters are essential for extracting cosmological information from galaxy surveys. Field-level analyses infer bias coefficients at a finite cutoff $\Lambda$, typically related to the lattice resolution, while $n$-point function analyses typically adopt renormalization conditions defined in the low-$k$ limit. In this work, we use the renormalization group (RG) to relate field-level measurements at different cutoffs and connect them to $n$-point function measurements. We generate mock galaxy fields with a Lagrangian perturbation theory forward model and a galaxy bias expansion, and then measure the bias parameters across a range of cutoffs. We show that the RG predictions describe the measured running and, in the limit $\Lambda\to 0$, agree with the (tree-level) $n$-point function measurements of first-order $b_\delta$ and second-order $b_{\delta^2}, b_{{G}_2}$. We also measure the running on halo catalogs based on full $N$-body simulations and show that the RG prediction describes the measurements well within the predicted systematic errors. Our results establish the RG flow as a natural formulation for relating galaxy bias measurements at different cutoffs and connecting the schemes used in field-level and $n$-point function analyses.

papers.title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
papers.abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

papers.title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
papers.abstract: The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass $M$ and the compactness $C\equiv M/R$. Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with $\Gamma = 2$ are stable only for $M\lesssim0.63$ and $C\lesssim0.25$, a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.

papers.title: Spacetime contactability in Galactic civilization networks: Contact counts and percolation
papers.abstract: The number of Galactic civilizations does not determine whether they are in contact. Allowing civilizations to appear at different times separates listening, audibility, mutual-listening, and relay networks, with a distinct reply-closing condition requiring a return signal within the sender's lifetime. For each network we derive the contact counts and estimate the connectivity threshold in a uniform population, then apply the results to a structured Galactic disc, separating the detection range $d_{\rm max}$ from the light horizon $cL$ through $\chi=d_{\rm max}/cL$. The contactability is $\eta=\pi n d_{\rm max}^{2}$, where $n$ is the active civilization surface density. Averaged over civilization appearances, the lifetime listening count is $2\eta$ for all $\chi$ and, at fixed detection range, for any lifetime distribution. Audibility and mutual-listening counts sum to $4\eta$, but connectivity depends on threshold behavior rather than counts alone. As $\chi\rightarrow0$, the listening threshold decreases from the coeval value $4.51$ to $1.32\pm0.01$. Assuming an ideal complete survey, our own non-detection gives the reference bound $\eta(R_0)\le2.75$ at the Sun's Galactocentric radius. This benchmark lies above the listening, audibility and relay thresholds throughout the range studied. Unlike the coeval model, the spacetime model can satisfy both this benchmark and a local connectivity criterion, moving the local-contact frontier outward by $3.2$ kpc. Under the same benchmark, civilizations hear at most $5.5$ others on average, while the mean reply-closing count falls below unity for $\chi\gtrsim1$. papers.title: Time Running Backwards, and Where It Stops: Superoscillations of Proper Time and the Memory of the Environment
papers.abstract: A quantum system prepared in a superposition of proper times - a clock whose worldline is superposed, or a clock at rest in a superposed gravitational potential - evolves, in each branch, by the same dynamics for a different duration. Post-selecting the control that sets the proper time turns the superposition into a superoscillation of the time-dilation factor: the system is found to have evolved for a proper time $\alpha_w t$, where the weak value $\alpha_w$ may exceed unity, vanish, or be negative - the quantum time-translation machine of Aharonov, Anandan, Popescu and Vaidman. We ask how far back such a machine can run an irreversible process. The test system is a sealed cell - excited atoms, the radiation field they emit into, and the absorbing walls, carried as one quantum object - and the witness is projective: atoms that had begun to decay before the run are found, in the post-selected sub-ensemble, more excited than when inserted. The answer is exact and depends only on the atoms' survival amplitude. With two branches the witness holds only while the decay is younger than the memory time of the environment, after which the emission becomes Markovian. Beyond it, the post-selection amplifies the minute difference between the contents of the cell in the two branches, set by the full energy spread of the atoms and their field rather than by the linewidth, and the witness fails. Reversing a decay past the memory time requires many branches, an environment with a strictly bounded spectrum, and a post-selection probability that falls exponentially with the number of environmental oscillations to be undone. The obstacle to reversal is therefore not entropy but bandwidth - the same bandwidth that makes the emission irreversible in the first place. We give four ways to superpose a clock rate, from hollow massive shells to inertial velocities.

papers.title: Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps
papers.abstract: HI intensity mapping is a promising probe of the large-scale structure of the Universe, but is limited by foregrounds and instrumental systematics. For the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) L-band data, it is found that emission line stacking measurement reveals a type of systematics related to the instrument beam. Using simulations with a full-sky electromagnetic beam model, we show that the chromaticity and sidelobes of the MeerKAT beam modulate the frequency-smooth foreground emission and introduce oscillating structures that persist after foreground removal. The beam rotates with respect to the sky between two types of scans, and combining datasets with different beam orientations before foreground cleaning makes the residuals stronger. In MeerKLASS L-band data, processing these two types of scans separately significantly suppresses the oscillating residuals while preserving the stacked HI signal. The ratio of the HI signal amplitude to the systematic fluctuation amplitude increases by 81%. We find an oscillating structure in PCA mode 11 in our previous data processing, but simply removing this mode does not improve the stacked spectrum due to the signal loss. Our strategy can help mitigate spectral ripples that are induced by the beam in future MeerKAT and SKA-Mid surveys.

papers.title: Aster: A Flexible and Robust Collection of Numerical Tools for N-Body Problems
papers.abstract: The Aster library is an open-source collection of numerical tools designed for large-scale gravitational N-body simulations. Aster provides a flexible environment to its users, enabling it to be used in the analysis of a broad range of astrophysical problems. The library implements efficient force calculation algorithms, including a spatial tree solver optimized with coordinate-dependent identifiers, which has been fine-tuned for both CPU and GPU architectures. Despite its high degree of modularity, many parts of the library have been optimized with SIMD instructions, heavy parallelization, and support on dedicated hardware. Aster also offers a wide variety of numerical symplectic integrators, such as SABA (from first to tenth order), the classic leapfrog algorithm, and the more advanced Wisdom-Holman (WH) integrator, while also providing a vast collection of mathematical tools, e.g., post-newtonian expansions (1PN, 2PN, 2.5PN), data collection and graphing systems, a built-in renderer, and presets for faster instantiation of large amounts of bodies. In this work we will discuss in depth the details of each module as well as the results of several performance- and accuracy-related tests, probing the library's capabilities in different physical applications.
